LET ME TOUCH YOU-Bob Crewe Generation 
-CGC 1000 
Here's the first release from the Bob 
Crewe Generation for some time and a fine 
set it is, too. Included are oldies like "Stella 
By Starlight," contemporary material such as 
Mancini's "Moon River" and "Two For The 
Road," and Bacharach's "Wives And Lovers." 
There's also a host of Bob Crewe penned 
songs like the title cut and the theme from 
"Barbarella." Each track is handled in an 
interesting manner and the LP should do 
well with MOR listeners. 
DEVOTION-John McLaughlin-Douglas 4 
After nearly a decade of studio work and 
limited notoriety, guitarist McLaughlin has 
burst into the spotlight with an album of 
superior musicianship. He is a master of his 
instrument but, more than that, he is an 
artist of unusual sensitivity-one who goes 
beyond the technique of playing to actually 
use the guitar as a means of articulating. All 
songs on this, his Douglas debut LP, are 
his own compositions; among the accompan- 
ists for the set, 
Buddy Miles and Larry 
Young. 
Exciting and original 
entry which 
should establish McLaughlin firmly. Album 
could spiral into a really sizeable item.

Album to watch.

The pressing and distribution of Lib- 
erty Records repertoire went back to 
EMI with effect from July 27th after 
talks to renegotiate the deal between 
Liberty and Philips had failed. There 
was a further nine months to run on 
the existing pact, but Liberty -UA 
London chief Martin Davis invoked a 
fail-safe clause in the contract to end 
the arrangement. Liberty thus re- 
turns to the EMI fold, where the UA 
label is already being handled, and 
the Liberty -UA sales force will now 
operate with both labels in the same 
rational neck of the woods. 
The 
agreement with EMI does not include 
the imported Blue Note jazz line or 
any tape or budget product. Davis 
was one of the indie chiefs most con- 
cerned by the horrendous hang-up 
that occurred at Phonodisk, the Phil- 
ips-Polydor 
distribution 
service, 
when it began its Ilford operation 
last Easter, but he has denied that 
this hiatus motivated the move of 
Liberty 
back 
to 
EMI. 
Philips - 
Phonodisk supremo Stephen Gottlieb 
confirmed that talks had started to 
renegotiate the Liberty -Philips deal 
but ended because the parties could 
not reach a mutually satisfactory 
financial arrangement. Davis fixed 
the pact with EMI in discussions with 
EMI Records managing director Phil- 
ip Brodie and sales and marketing 
chief Cliff Busby in which he was 
joined by Liberty -UA legal and ac- 
counting vp Sy Zucker. 
Recent activity at United Artists 
Music publishing companies indicates 
a surge of important releases be- 
tween now and the autumn. On the 
film music front singles and albums 
include the soundtrack of "Ned Kel- 
ly" which features a track by Mick 
Jagger, all other music composed by 
Shel Silverstein. Later in the year 
two major United Artists films are 
"The Private Life of Sherlock Hol- 
mes" with score by Miklos Rosza and 
"The Music Lovers" based on the life 
of Tchaikovsky with Andre Previn 
conducting the 
London Symphony 
Orchestra. Other future productions 
are "The Landlords" music by Al 
Kooper; "Cotton Comes to Harlem" 
score by Galt McDermot and "Good- 
bye Mr. Tibbs" music by Quincy 
Jones and Dave Grusin. Noel Rogers 
is excited about the current success 
of 
Shirley 
Bassey's 
version 
of 
"Something" and forecasts her Sep- 
tember album will reveal a new inter- 
pretation of contemporary, standard 
and original material. Of "Oh Calcut- 
ta," Rogers is of the opinion that it 
could be the most exciting musical 
review to arrive in London for many 
years. 
The days of open-air pop festivals 
seem to be numbered, judging by re- 
cent events. The upcoming event in 
the Isle of Wight is encountering 
difficulties in finalising a site which 
may culminate in a legal injunction 
to stop the fest taking place at all. 
At a recent public meeting in Fresh- 
water to discuss the event Brigadier 
C. G. Phipps, a county councillor, 
was howled down by a contingent of 
hippies as he tried to chair the meet- 
ing and ended up wrestling for the 
microphone with festival producer 
Rikki Farr of Fiery Creations. Island 
authorities have threatened an in- 
junction if agreement is not reached 
with Fiery Creations on festival ar- 
rangements. Meanwhile a storm of 
protest has arisen about the recent 
blues festival which took place at 
Shepton Mallet, Somerset, on the 
Bath and West Agricultural Society's 
showground. The National Farmers 
Union is complaining to the Home 
Secretary about damage done to the 
ground and the amount of garbage 
left behind, and also because a farm- 
er whose property is adjacent lost 
five hundred fencing posts and seven 
gates. The NFU is also considering 
action against members who lease 
their land for pop festivals, on ac- 
count of such hiring out for non- 
agricultural purposes of profit is 
unethical in view of the agricultural 
subsidies being paid to farmers by 
the state. The Hollywood festival in 
Staffordshire has left several credi- 
tors with egg on their faces and a 
Conservative Member of Parliament 
is seeking legal measures to stop the 
forthcoming Plumpton festival from 
taking place on behalf of objecting 
local residents. A free concert was 
staged in Hyde Park July 18th by 
Blackhill Entertainments and attend- 
ed by an estimated 50,000. It was 
marred by several ugly incidents, 
mostly caused by Hell's Angels, the 
self appointed stewards, and a hot 
dog stand overturned, giving first de- 
gree burns to a girl who was taken 
to the nearby St. George's Hospital 
in company with ten other young- 
sters on bad trips. It seems debatable 
whether the Greater London Council 
will continue to grant permission for 
these mass pop happenings in Hyde 
Park in view of these incidents and 
the underlying current of violence at 
this last concert, plus the growing 
hostility throughout the areas select- 
ed as venues for such events. 
John Morton was elected general 
secretary of the Musicians Union in 
succession to Hardie Ratcliffe, who 
retires next 
spring. Morton 
will 
resign his post as senior lecturer in 
industrial relations and administra- 
tion at Solihull Technical College at 
the end of the year and will have a 
major task on his hands when com- 
mercial radio is officially introduced 
here. He has already stipulated that 
commercial stations must use a fair 
share of live music in addition to 
records in their programming, and a 
lot of hard bargaining obviously lies 
ahead on needle time allocation. A 
July 1st increase of 33% in recording 
fees for musicians in the dance band 
and light orchestra categories means 
that the session rate has risen by £3 
to £12. 
EMI 
group 
managing 
director 
John Read denied Israeli allegations 
that the company had bowed to pres- 
sure from Arab countries in ending 
its disk pressing arrangement in Is- 
rael with the Palestine Orient compa- 
ny. The move resulted in a ban being 
imposed by Israeli Commerce Indus- 
try officials on the import of all EMI 
records. Read explained the termina- 
tion of the deal with Palestine Orient 
was in purely commercial grounds 
because EMI was not satisfied with 
merchandising arrangements.

Stig Anderson's 10th Anniversary 
LONDON - Stig 
Anderson 
of 
Sweden Music AB is celebrating his 
10th anniversary in the Scandinavian 
publishing and record field. He began 
his publishing activities in 1960 after 
having a hit as a songwriter with 
"Klas-Goran," and also opened up 
the Scandinavian outlet on Bens Mu- 
sic in Brussels, as well as acquiring 
American and European catalogs. In 
1965, he began his own record label 
Polar Music AB in partnership with 
Bengt 
Bernhag 
which 
established 
many local artistes, and also has 
publishing and record interests in 
Denmark and Norway. In 1969, And- 
erso 1 was awarded a Swedish "Gram- 
my" for the best local lyr'c-writer.

CBS Talent Roster Highlights 
Sales Convention In Freeport 
FREEPORT, BAHAMAS-The pre- 
sentation of local foreign recordings 
formed one of the high points of CBS 
International's 
Freeport, 
Bahamas 
meetings last week. CBS subsidiaries 
from various parts of the world show- 
cased samples of their newest pop 
and classical product for other CBS 
International Convention delegates as 
well as for Columbia Records person- 
nel. 
The A&R presentations came at the 
end of two days of general business 
meetings. These were attended by 54 
CBS 
International 
representatives 
from the New York headquarters, 
and from overseas operational offices 
and local subsidiaries. 
Latin America 
From Latin America, both CBS Ar- 
gentina and CBS Mexico served up 
samples of the latest kinds of music 
happening to the south of the U. S. 
Argentina presented records by the 
artists who currently are on the local 
charts: 
Sandro, 
Leonardo 
Favio, 
Piero, Los Naufragos, and Fedra y 
Maximiliano. At the same time, they 
introduced two new young talents:

tapes 
to introduce the 
music of 
Vicente 
Fernandes, 
Sonora 
San- 
tanera, Las Ventanas, Mario y su De-

Film Music Upsurge In Japan; King 
Offers `Definitive' 7 -LP Package 
HOLLYWOOD - Japan is the most 
rapidly growing record market in the 
world. 'It should soon be second to 
the U. S., topping even Great Bri- 
tain's burgeoning sales. This, 
ac- 
cording to Ron Eyre, deputy director 
of Liberty-U.A.'s International divi- 
sion and Patrick Boyle, L. A. office 
International manager for the labels, 
can be directly attributed to that na- 
tion's fascination for and tremendous 
interest in the western way of life. 
"Baseball was probably the first 
indication 
of that interest," says 
Eyre. But our western flicks started 
to catch on in the 50's. It now encom- 
passes a variety of western cultures. 
And particularly classical, jazz and 
motion picture music." 
"Japan probably does more with a 
movie soundtrack album than any 
country outside the U. S., occasional- 
ly outstripping the states," 
says 
Boyle. He points to "Battle of Bri- 
tain" as an example. The soundtrack 
LP outsold both Britain and the U. 
S. "Man and a Woman" topped the 
Eurovision Contest Revisions 
Aim At Reviving Fest Interest 
LONDON - Major changes will be 
made in the organization of next 
year's Eurovision Song Contest to be 
held April 3rd at the Gaiety Theater, 
Dublin. 
Staging the event at an estimated 
cost of £10,000 will be Radio Telefis 
Eireann, and the different set-up is 
being introduced 
to overcome the 
controversies and disagreements of 
past Eurovision tournys which have 
caused several countries to drop out 
and also revive a waning public in- 
terest in the event. The 1971 juries 
will consist of two members only 
from each country instead of the ten 
used hitherto. One juror must be un- 
der 25 years old, and the other above 
that age level, but none will be per- 
mitted under 18 or over 60. Each 
juror will have five votes and will 
award each song in points out of five 
and for the first time in the contest's 
history, the juries will attend the 
event instead of voting by radio tele- 
phone. Their travelling expenses will 
be paid by the countries they rep- 
resent but this will be the only pay- 
ment they will receive. 
Public Exposure 
The public will be able to hear all 
the contesting songs before the actu- 
al vocal joust takes place by means 
of telerecordings made by the partici- 
pants. 
Nimbus 9/RCA Productions Increase 
TORONTO - Nimbus 
9 and RCA 
have been working so closely togeth- 
er it's only natural they are being 
regarded as a team of one. 
Jack Richardson, one of the princi- 
ples of Nimbus 9 and producer of the 
Guess Who, has been cranking out 
productions under both labels. His 
anchor group, The Guess Who from 
Winnipeg, are now making the big 
chart noise with their recent release, 
"Hand Me Down World." On the do- 
mestic front RCA has just released a 
couple of Bill Misener productions 
that could shake the recording scene. 
The disk having the most potential 
would appear to be ".I Don't Believe" 
by Vancouver's Canada. The plug 
side was written by group organist 
Clyde Harvey. Formerly Fox, this 
group have found an eager following 
throughout Upper Canada and are 
currently on a tour of the Western 
Provinces. The disc has already been 
picked up by radio stations in the 
areas in which they are known. 
Also a big plus for Misener is his 
production of "In 
The Rain" by 
Tranquillity Base, a strong follow-up 
to their "If You're Lookin"' deck. An 
interesting switch was the RCA To- 
ronto studios' recording session by 
Montreal's French Revolution. Out of 
this has come "The Dawn Of The 
Revolution" with the orchestration 
and arrangements by Misener. Otta- 
wa's Marshmallow Group have also 
come up with a Misner production in 
"Sing To 
My Lover" written by 
group member Tim Eaton and their 
manager Vern Craig. Misener is a 
producer for RCA's Sun -Bar Produc- 
tions.

7 LP's, 84 Songs 
This week, King Records, U.A.'s 
licensee in the Orient, will be releas- 
ing what Eyre terms is the "defini- 
tive" collection of film themes, It will 
certainly be the most ambitious al- 
bum set in the history of soundtrack 
and film music, including 84 songs on 
seven 
LP's, handsomely packaged 
with a 100 page four-color hard cov- 
er book -brochure. Set, titled "Gala 
Collection of Screen Music," includes 
three U. A. LP's featuring the music 
of Leroy Holmes, two Seven Seas 
and two London disks. 
A similar 
package of five additional LP's is 
currently in preparation. Eyre says 
there are no plans to release the 
same product in the U. S., since dup- 
lication here would 
be financially 
prohibitive. 
The project was undertaken as a 
result of what Eyre terms Japan's 
"total involvement" in film songs. 
Double album sets like U. A.'s film 
themes to the James Bond features 
average 
between 
25-30 
thousand 
units. "There is a much closer liason 
between film distribs and record firms 
in Japan than here," says Eyre, "ad- 
ding to the escalation of film album 
project sales."

Note jazz acts such as Jimmy Smith 
and Ornette Coleman are enormous 
record names in Japan.

Brit. At MIDEM: 
Bd Of Trade Sets 
Lower Subsidy 
LONDON - The Board of Trade 
subsidy for British partipants in the 
1971 MIDEM meet has been reduced 
by approximately 150. The primary 
reason is that the Board has to sup- 
port other industries in a similar 
fashion and the £50,000 it spent on 
the 1970 MIDEM was the second 
highest total it has ever invested 
in a trade fair. Smaller companies 
prepared to share office accommoda- 
tion in pairs will still be able to 
attend without 
cash outlay. 
The 
equivalent of two entire floors of the 
Palais des Festivals at Cannes has 
already been booked by disk and pub- 
lishing companies from all over the 
world including 35 British firms.

The Japanese music industry, the 
2nd -world wide market of the world 
today, is bringing up such new labels 
as Toho, Pop, Canyon, and Pioneer 
this year and simultaneously they 
are getting ready to sell the 1st com- 
positions for a large demand in the 
coming year. In addition, there is an 
outstanding personal transfer-young 
recording directors and sales promo- 
ters from companies of established 
fame. Some foreign recording firms 
are 
striking into the market of 
Japan which has been raised with 
pure domestic capital. Therefore, it 
seems that the sales activity of the 
commercial field toward the coming 
year-end will be engaged in a con- 
fused free fight among established 
firms and new ones. 
Toho Records is a subsidiary com- 
pany of Toho Movie Co., which is 
famous for its movie and drama pro- 
ductions all over the world. It is 
scheduled to make up catalogs main- 
ly consisting of singing film actors 
and actresses in order to release its 
1st records arranged by directors 
and sales promoters moved from its 
movie division on 1st of October. 
Pop Records, a Nippon Victor and 
Bunka Broadcasting !Co., joint-stock 
enterprise will 
cultivate the new 
broadcasting fan through the TV and 
radio program. 
Canyon Records, founded by the 
stock introduction of Pony (Pres- 
ident: Tatsuro Ishida), a subsidiary 
firm of the Nippon Broadcasting 
Co., will be managed by Takanori 
Kamata (former production dept. di- 
rector and representative to manager 
of recording operation). Six direc- 
tors, five sales promoters and two 
advisers from Nippon Columbia Co., 
already have transferred from Nip- 
pon Columbia Co., and a fairly large 
number of salesmen will be added be- 
fore the establishing day of August 
3 and this is a "Standing Menace" to 
every records company. 
Pioneer Records is about to be es- 
tablished by Pioneer, a maker of 
sound parts and Watanable Produc- 
tion and it has such labels abroad as 
Waner, Ripleese and Atlantic dis- 
tributed by Watanabe's source. How- 
ever, one difficulty in the personal 
organization 
in Pioneer 
is 
that 
Hizuru Kaneko (former manager of 
foreign 
dept. 
division) 
suddenly 
changed his idea to enter into Toshi- 
ba Records, though he is supposed to 
work at the post of managing big 
foreign labels. Instead, Atsutaka To- 
rio is marked out for the post of 
managing them. However, Japanese 
music industry will be dividing the 
power into wings-one is established 
firms of fame founded by makers of 
acoustic parts-the other, the radio 
and TV production capacity which 
takes advantage of music tapes and 
video production is wildly going into 
the recording industry. A few minor 
record companies will be joining the 
market at the end of this year.

Bandana Signs 
Humble Pie In 
1st Global Deal 
NEW YORK - Dee Anthony, man- 
aging director of Bandana Enter- 
prises, has signed Humble Pie for 
worldwide representation in personal 
management. 
While Bandana has been instru- 
mental in building English artists 
such as Ten Years After, Jethro Tull, 
Savoy Brown and King Crimson in 
the capacity of North American per- 
sonal manager, this marks the com- 
pany's first involvement with an En- 
glish artist on a worldwide basis. 
Bandana retains its interests in the 
North American management of Joe 
Cocker and Island Artists. 
Humble Pie, signed to A&M Rec- 
ords for the U. S., the United King- 
dom and Canada for a reported $400,- 
000 recently, consists of Steve Marri- 
ott, Peter Frampton, Greg Ridley and 
Jerry 
Shirley. 
Marriott, 
formerly 
lead singer with the Small Faces, 
shares the vocals with Frampton, 
former lead singer with The Herd, 
and Ridley, a one-time member of 
spooky Tooth. Drummer Shirley and 
bassist Ridley form the rhythm sec- 
tion with Frampton performing the 
majority of the solo guitar work. 
Marriott plays guitar, piano, organ 
and harmonica. 
The group has just completed its 
second album, scheduled for release 
in the United Kingdom today, Mon- 
day August 3rd. The LP will be re- 
leased in the U. S. Aug. 10 in con- 
encetion with Humbl Pie's first major 
U. S. tour under the Bandana banner 
which begins in September. Prior to 
their American tour, they will per- 
form Aug. 
2 
and 
4 at London's 
Round -house and Marquee and play 
Copenhagen Aug. 21-22 before head- 
lining at A&M's Waburn Abbey dis- 
tributor meeting September 8th. 
In a simultaneous announcement, 
Anthony stated that Humble Pie will 
be represented in the agency field 
exclusively by Premier Talent for the 
United States and _Canada. Said An- 
thony, "False and misleading state- 
ments have appeared in print to the 
affect that other agencies are in 
volved in Humble Pie's career. For 
the record, Premier Talent represents 
the group." 
Anthony 
and 
Frank 
Barsalona, 
President of Premier Talent, were in 
London last week (3) to meet with 
the members of ,Humble .Pie. While 
there, Anthony and Barsalona will 
also be meeting with -Island Records 
chief Chris Blackwell and the direc- 
tors of Island Artists in connection 
with upcoming U. S. tours by Island 
artists Traffic, Mott The Hoople, who 
had a highly successful first tour, and 
Free, who currently have the number 
one single and number two album in 
England. 
McNamara's Hit 
Launches Album 
NEW YORK - Paramount Rec- 
ord; Is rush releasing Robin McNa- 
mara's first album, on Steed Records, 
following up his current top ten sin- 
gle, "Lay A Little Lovin' On Me". 
The album, same title as the single, 
was produced by Jeff Barry. 
McNamara, who is currently ap- 
pearing in the lead male role in the 
Broadway production of "Hair," will 
tour extensively in support of the 
album as he did in promoting the 
single. 
Paramount, which distributes Steed, 
is 
preparing 
an 
indepth 
mar- 
keting and promo campaign for the 
album including extensive time buys 
and local advertising on a city by 
city basis as well as a national adver- 
tising publicity and promo campaign.

U.K. on their first LP. Famous Music president William P. Gallagher (second 
from r.) and director of business affairs Neil C. Reshen (far r.) returned to 
the U.S. from a recent services of meetings in England with Affinity's man- 
agement who, in the person's of Ronnie Scott (far 1.) and Peter Chipperfield 
(seated), came to N.Y. to sign a Paramount contract for the group. Standing 
(second from 1.) is Famous executive v.p. Jack Wiedenmann. 
Inez Foxx Goes 
Out As A Solo 
NEW YORK - Inez Foxx, Dynamo 
recording artist, will be appearing as 
a single in all future performances, 
both in person and on recordings. 
She had 
been working with her 
brother for the past few years as 
Inez and Charlie Foxx. Together they 
hit with such hit records as "Mockin' 
Bird," "Hurt By Love," "Ask Me," 
"Hi Diddle Diddle," "He's the One 
Inez recently returned from Eng- 
land, where she made her debut as a 
single with her new act. Dynamo, a 
division of Musicor Records, will re- 
lease a brand new record shortly 
featuring her in her recording debut 
as a single performer.

Viewlex Acquires 
RCA's 16mm Line 
HOLBROOK, NEW YORK - View- 
lex will acquire RCA's 16MM motion 
picture projector line designed pri- 
marily for educational and training 
The purchase 
price 
of approx- 
imately $5 million includes projectors 
presently in inventory, parts invento- 
ry, 
patents, 
engineering 
designs, 
manufacturing drawings, test equip- 
ment, tooling and a quantity of pro- 
jectors to be manufactured for View- 
lex by RCA, according to Ben Peirez, 
president and chairman of the Board 
of 
Viewlex, Inc. 
and 
Andrew 
F. 
Inglis, division vice president and 
general manager of RCA Commercial 
Electronic Systems. 
The agreement does not include 
other projector products such as TV 
Broadcast Station 16MM projectors, 
which will continue to be manufac- 
tured, 
marketed 
and 
serviced 
by 
RCA. No RCA plant facilities are 
involved in the transaction. 
Following delivery 
of the units 
still to be produced by RCA, Viewlex 
will commence manufacturing of the 
projectors in Holbrook, New York, 
where an additional 140,000 square 
feet of plant space is under construc- 
tion Peirez said.

Ross, Stein 
Manage Brethren 
NEW YORK - Brethren, the four - 
man group on Tiffany Records, a 
Scepter 
Records 
affiliate, 
is 
now 
managed 
by 
Murray 
Ross 
and 
Howard Stein's management compa- 
ny, Galileo. Ross is the president of 
Idea Planning Associates, the compa- 
ny creates all the advertising and 
public relations for Scepter. Stein is 
the producer of the Capitol Theatre 
in Port Chester, New York. 
Brethren is the only progressive 
rock act recording for the Scepter 
complex. Scepter and Tiffany, there- 
fore, are taking particular interest in 
launching Brethren's career. 
Ross 
plans to utilize all his advertising 
and publicity ability to asssist the 
band in establishing itself. 
Brethren is composed of four musi- 
cians: Tom Cosgrove - Guitars, lead 
vocal; Stu Woods - Bass, vocals; 
Rick Marotta - drums, vocals; Mike 
Garson - organ and piano. 
Galileo does not intend to take on 
any other groups in the foreseeable 
future. 
Berlin Rock Teams 
Coming To U.S.; 
Prophesy Albums 
HOLLYWOOD - In 
conjunction 
with the release a German rock LP in 
this country, Prophesy Records' pres- 
ident Mickey Shapiro has announced 
plans to bring two West Berlin rock 
acts - Amon Duul and Birth Control 
- to this country in the fall. 
Birth Control, whose first LP titled 
"Birth Control" was released last 
Monday (3), will arrive in the U. S. 
in early Oct. and embark on a four - 
week tour which is being set by Uni- 
versal Attractions of New York. Sev- 
en cities have been scheduled thus 
far. They are New York, Boston, 
Philadelphia, Chicago, Atlanta, San 
Francisco and Los Angeles. Prophesy 
is also working with Universal in 
setting TV dates in both L. A. and 
New York to coincide with the tour. 
In early No. Amon Duul, the la- 
bel's second German act, will arrive 
for a tour that will run through the 
second week in Sept. Amon Duul's 
first LP is slated for release late this 
month. 
Prophesy is distributed in the U. S. 
and Canada by Bell. The label's first 
LP, "Black Pearl `Live'," was re- 
leased last month. 
Campus Artists 
Forms A Label 
NEW YORK - Campus Artist Con- 
sultants, Ltd. has formed a label of 
the same name, reports Gene Frank, 
president. 
The 
parent 
company 
formed two publishing 
comnanies, 
Campus Artist Music Group (ASCAP) 
and Campus Artist Tunes (BMI), last 
Jan. The label expects to issue its 
first LP in Sept. Patrick West -Assoc. 
has been named the label's public 
relations firm. 
Vera Lynn Inks 
Stanyan Pact 
HOLLYWOOD - Vera Lynn, the 
English songstress, has signed an ex- 
clusive record contract with Stanyan 
Record head Rod McKuen for the 
United States and Canada. She will 
continue to be represented on EMI 
throughout the world, with her rec- 
ords produced in England by Harry 
Lewis. 
Her first Stanyan release will be an 
album slated for release in Oct.

Moody Blues 
Cop 1st Gold 
NEW YORK - The Moody Blues 
have been certified for their first gold 
album. Certification was confirmed 
this week by the Record Industry As- 
sociation of America (RIAA) for to 
"Our Children's Children's Children," 
on the Moody Blues' own Threshold 
label, nationally distributed by Lon- 
don Records. Gold records will be 
awarded to Justin Hayward, Graeme 
Edge, Mike Pinder, Ray Thomas, 
John Lodge and their producer, Tony 
Clarke. 
Previous Moody Blues material ap- 
peared on Deram Records. Several of 
the group's earlier LP's are now clos- 
ing in on the gold record level of 
$1,000.000 in sales with certification 
possible within the next 
several 
weeks. 
Meanwhile, the group is now ex- 
pected back in the United States for 
a brief tour. Anticipated dates await- 
ing confirmation from London are 
September 17 to 27, during which the 
group will be working every night in 
a different city. Tour is being set by 
CMA. 
Blues 'Rides' Gold 
NEW YORK - The Blues Image 
have earned their first gold record 
when their Atco single, "Ride Cap- 
tain Ride" certified as a million seller 
by the Record Industry Association 
of America (RIAA). "Ride" was tak- 
en from the Blues Image second al- 
bum on Atco, "Open," which was is- 
sued last Jan. It was released as a 
single after it broke out of the LP. 
The Blues Image, now on a nation- 
al tour, will make their first appear- 
ance at the Fillmore East later this 
month (21 & 22). 
Plumb Single Has 
An Intl Flavor 
LOS ANGELES - Producer Neely 
Plumb has created an "international" 
single combining an Italian melody, 
English language lyrics, British in- 
strumentalists, Italian chorus and an 
American lead singer. 
The single is "The Fortune Cookie 
Song" which IMC Productions, for 
whom Plumb works, will place with a 
record company for distribution. 
The song was written in Italy, ac- 
cording to Plumb and became a hit in 
Japan several months ago as sung by 
a young girl. Plumb received exclu- 
sive rights from its publisher, Peer 
Southern, to create a record for the 
U. S. market. While in London sever- 
al months ago, Plumb had a lyric 
written and cut the orchestral track 
with 26 pieces conducted by Nicky 
Welsh. 
From London, he went to Rome on 
business and located a children's 
chorus to sing an Italian refrain 
which runs through the song. That 
was added onto the tracks in Rome. 
Then when he returned to Los Ange- 
les, 
he 
recorded his 
12 -year 
old 
daughter Eve, as the lead voice.

Tannen has also been coordinating 
the recording of several recent label 
pactees, including John D. Louder- 
milk, Tom Paxton and Janie & Den- 
nis, who are being produced by Peter 
Asher, Milt Okun and Jerry Corbett 
respectively. 
Due to the unprecedented growth 
rate of Warner Bros./Reprise over 
the past year, the New York office 
has been constantly reviewing new 
acts, masters, Broadway and off- 
Broadway shows. In addition, Tannen 
and members of his staff have been 
scouting new talent along the eastern 
seaboard and Canada. 
Reprise Readies 
Hendrix -Redding LP 
BURBANK - An album of per- 
formances by Otis Redding and the 
Jimi Hendrix Experience at the Mon- 
terey International Pop Festival is 
being prepared for mid -August re- 
lease by Reprise Records. 
Producer Lou Adler gave the com- 
pany rights to the performances un- 
der an agreement negotiated by Mo 
Ostin, president of Warner 
Bros. 
Records. Lou Adler and John Phillips 
produced the festival and the album, 
which is titled, "Otis Redding/The 
Jimi 
Hendrix 
Experience/Historic 
Performances Recorded at the Mon- 
terey Pop Festival." 
Parts of the Monterey tapes were 
used for the soundtrack of "Monterey 
Pop," a documentary film of the 
event, but none of the musical mate- 
rial from the festival has previously 
been available on records. 
Otis Redding's performance on the 
record includes his in -person versions 
of "Shake," "Respect," "I've Been 
Loving You Too Long," "Satisfac- 
tion" and "Try a Little Tenderness." 
The Jimi Hendrix Experience is 
captured in its first United States 
appearance, a show which included 
"Like a Rolling Stone," "Rock Me, 
Baby," "Can You See Me" and "Wild 
Thing"-the latter song a seven - 
minute version which 
ended with 
Hendrix setting fire to his guitar. 
Warner Bros. plans a large-scale 
advertising, 
promotion 
and 
sales 
campaign to accompany the release 
of the album, according 
to Stan 
Cornyn, the company's director of 
creative services. 
Cornyn said the campaign, which 
includes extensive radio and print ad- 
vertising and special merchandising 
aids, is one of the largest in the 
history of the company. 
B.B. King, Mgr. 
Open Prod. Co. 
NEW YORK - B. B. King, ABC/ 
Dunhill recording artist has formed 
a 
record 
production 
company 
in 
partnership with his manager, Sid- 
ney A. Seidenberg. First act signed 
by the company is a two -man blues 
group, Malcolm and Chris, both 19 
years old. It is also the first act, since 
B. B. King himself, to be added to 
Seidenberg's artist management firm, 
Sidney A. Seidenberg, Inc. 
In managing Malcolm and Chris 
Seidenberg will use the same formula 
that has proved successful with B. B. 
King. This includes, Seidenberg says, 
heavy promotion and publicity aimed 
at the youth market. 
Malcolm and Chris were discovered 
last year in Dayton, Ohio by B. B. 
King while he was playing an en- 
gagement there. Their first LP, "Just 
The Blues," is scheduled for release 
in early August, on the BluesTime 
label.

Studio One Bows 
CHICAGO -A new sound recording 
studio facility opened in Chicago at 
25 East Chestnut this week, and ac- 
cording 
to 
owner Kirk 
Johnson. 
"Studio One fills Chicago's increasing 
need for a high quality, production - 
oriented sound recording facility." 
Although Studio One boasts many 
client "creature comforts" such as a 
billiard room, color TV and swim- 
ming pool, according to Johnson, 
"there's a lot of serious thought, 
careful planning and thorough design 
that we've put into the business end 
of this place." 
Although Studio One's clientelle 
consists mostly of advertising agen- 
cies and other radio and TV commer- 
cial producers, it offers complete au- 
dio recording facilities, duplication 
and other sound services to program 
syndicators, education sound pack- 
agers and industrial audio aid pro- 
ducers. 
Special Agent Bows 
NEW YORK - Special Agent Music, 
a publishing firm with BMI affilia- 
tion, has been established as a sub- 
sidiary of Lip Enterprises. Hamilton 
Peyton would head up the new com- 
pany. 
Special Agent Music has a cata- 
logue of 25 songs mostly written by 
Monk Higgins and Bernice Leena for 
Helena Hollins, singer under contract 
to Stonegood Records. Her first al- 
bum, "The Name of The Game." will 
be released later this month. Ten of 
the tunes in the album were penned 
by Higgins and Leena. 
BN's McDuff LP 
`Somthing Special' 
HOLLYWOOD - Liberty/UA, Inc. 
will release a special Blue Note al- 
bum, "To Seek A New Home," by 
Brother Jack McDuff, in addition to 
its scheduled August release. 
Frank Wolff, McDuff's producer 
and head of Blue Note Records, said: 
"After Jimmy Smith, the market was 
glutted 
with 
would-be 
organists, 
most of whom made little contribu- 
tion to music. Brother Jack is an 
important exception, and this album 
will again prove his wide -spread ap- 
peal to jazz, R&B, and rock listeners, 
both fans and critics." 
Music Fair USA Set 
NASHVILLE - Sept., 5-6-7 has been 
designated as the dates for the Sec- 
ond Annual Music and Crafts Fair to 
be held in Benton, Kentucky. The 
Music Fair, a contest in rock, pop, 
and country music, is expected to 
draw contestants and fans from the 
entire United States. The huge open 
air stage will accommodate three mu- 
sical organizations at one time and 
judging will be done by Music City's 
top personalities. Cash and merchan- 
disie prizes will be given, plus rec- 
ording contracts. 
Contest rules may be abtained by 
writing Music and Crafts Fair USA, 
Benton, Kentucky, 42025.

produeerspt'oIIle 
An indie producer's survival does 
not soley depend on knowing where 
it's at today, but also on his ability 
to visualize the trends of tomorrow. 
Lewis Merenstein, very much a part 
of today's 
music scene, 
has an in- 
teresting viewpoint on the upcoming 
new leisure -time industry, the audio- 
visual cartridge. He'd like to get on 
the 
bandwagon by adapting today's 
beleagered rock fest picture for audio- 
visual cartridge use. That is, if kids 
can't see their 
favorite 
performers 
"live," then the next best thing might 
be to produce rock fests on audio- 
visual tapes, a sort of home "Wood- 
stock" approach. 
Merenstein, however, is very busy 
with non -visual musical presentations 
via records and tapes. His firm, In- 
herit Productions, is stocked with fine 
contemporary 
talent 
who 
turn 
to 
Merenstein for their recording sessions. 
They include Van Morrison, Country 
Joe 
& 
the 
Fish, 
Miriam 
Makeba, 
Dorothy 
Morrison, 
Turley 
Richards 
and, most recently, Biff Rose. 
The indie producer, a large, genial 
man, moved into the production scene 
about 21/2 years ago, after "enjoying 
watching producers have the respon- 
sibility of choosing 
artists, material 
and arrangements" from the vantage 
point of being 
a recording engineer 
on a free-lance basis for eight years. 
He started his new career by cutting 
such artists as Barry Goldberg and 
Charlie Musselwhite. 
Merenstein, observing the business 
with dedication, feels that there's too 
much product being released, a condi- 
tion that doesn't allow enough con- 
centration on artists. 
LEWIS MERENSTEIIN 
He feels that AM radio 
is pretty 
much "messed up" because it's "too 
contained, too Madison Ave -oriented." 
While he's thankful for FM, he sees the 
danger of a change in format tha: re- 
sult from increased advertising in the 
medium, thus lessening the amount 
of product exposed. 
A 
musician 
(he 
played 
trumpet) 
Merenstein's producing functions also 
include arranging and some writing of 
material. He regards music and films 
as the -honest media." First came 
music, 
he said, and when the film 
world caaght on with indie productions 
in its own area, films, too, evolved into 
a "honest media."

Basic Album Inventory

attention to key catalog, top steady selling LP's, as well as recent chart hits still going strong in sales. Information is supplied by manufacturers. This is a weekly 
revolving list presented in alphabetical order. It is advised that this card be kept until the list returns to this alphabetical section.

Capitol Inks Brennan 
HOLLYWOOD-Capitol Records has 
announced 
the signing of Michael 
Brennan. In the mid -Fifties he sang 
with his mother and his brother in 
a group called the Nash Family Trio. 
Brennan's first single for Capitol 
will be a tune titled "First Day in 
the World Without Her," to be re- 
leased in the next few weeks. He is 
managed by the Sam Riddle -Nick 
Brainard Companies.

industry people who participated in Jimmy Bowen's 4th Annual Amos Invi- 
tational Golf Tournament and gala fest at Los Robles Course in Thousand 
Oaks, Cal. (Aug. 8-10). Left to right Bobby Goldsboro, Andy Williams, Glen 
Campbell, and Tommy Roe. Trophy winners in the two day event: 1st place, 
Team Event-Bob Murphy/Jack Grimes. 2nd place-Don Lanier/Bill Casady. 
1st Individual Low Gross-Andy Williams. 2nd I.L.G.-Jack Grimes. 1st Indiv. 
Low Net-Peter Townsend. 2nd I.L.N.-Piggy Smith. Longest Drive-Red 
Steagell. Closest To Hole-Chuck Blore. Longest Drive With Putter-Gene 
Weed. Putting Contest-Don Carter. Drinking Trophy-Leroy Pearson. Club 
Throwing Contest-Tommy Roe. Trophies awarded for all events. Prizes as 
follows: Travelling Honda & Divorce Machine won by Budd Dolinger; 1948

Capitol's Studio `A' 
Opens In Hollywood 
HOLLYWOOD-Capitol Records is 
officially 
opening 
its 
remodeled 
Studio "A" with a party Thursday 
evening, (20), to he attended by rep- 
resentatives of Hollywood advertis- 
ing agencies and production firms. 
A unique feature of the up -dated 
studio is a 16 -track console consid- 
ered the most advanced of any cur- 
rently in use. Tle console was con- 
structed by Quad 8 of North Holly- 
wood to 
specifications supplied by 
Capitol's 
Recording 
Department 
headed by Peter Dent. 
A door prize at Thursday's party 
will be a three-hour recording session 
employing the 16 -track console. 
Capitol's 
remodeled 
Studio "A"' 
will be available to outside producers 
through the label's Custom Services 
Division.

Prophesy In Phase 2 Of A&R Concept 
LOS ANGELES - Prophesy Records 
has begun "Phase II' of its A&R 
plans with the signing of four new 
acts and the launching of East Coast 
production 
plans. Prophesy's 
first 
phase was the acquisition of product 
from artists outside the label-Amon

five volumn Blues series. 
Fantasy Signs Abel 
OAKLAND - Fantasy Records has 
announced the first in a series of new 
talent acquisitions. Abel, a San Fran- 
cisco rock band has inked a long 
term pact with Fantasy, according to 
Saul Zaentz, president, and is al- 
ready at work on the album. 
Abel takes its name from Abel 
Sanchez, the lead singer and guitarist 
who also writes and arranges the 
group's material. They have been to- 
gether as a unit for three years and 
have been working in San Francisco 
steadily during the past year at clubs 
and dances. 
Drummer with the group is Tommy 
Catalano, youngest of a long time 
San Francisco musical family whose 
members have played with Woody 
Herman and Stan Kenton, and which 
included 
Billy 
Catalano, 
veteran 
executive with the musician's union. 
David Spedicci, tenor, and Lawrence 
Chiesa, trumpet, make up the horn 
section, and bassist is Charles Bolds. 
Fantasy producer Ray Shanklin is 
working with Abel now at the Wally 
Heider Studio in San Francisco on 
the initial tracks of their first LP. 
300 Compete In 
Atkins Festival 
NASHVILLE - The first annual 
Chet Atkins Guitar Festival con- 
cluded with eight young American 
guitarists winning a total of $6,000 
in award money. The festival was 
held in Nashville the nights of August 
7 and 8, the festival marked the 
realization 
of 
a 
life-long 
dream 
cherished by Atkins to help young 
musicians get a start. 
Over three hundred guitar players 
from thirty-six states and four foreign 
countries, between the ages of 14 
and 25 submitted tapes 
of their 
work to a board of judges. From 
these, sixteen semi-finalists were se- 
lected to come to Nashville to com- 
pete in the finals. In Nashville, the 
number was narrowed down to four 
electric and four acoustical players. 
Each group was presented to the 
audience on separate evenings during 
the nearly four-hour concerts featur- 
ing Jerry 
Reed, 
Boots Randolph, 
Floyd Cramer, Kenny Rogers and the 
First Edition, Pete Fountain, Chet 
Atkins, and the Nashville Pops Or- 
chestra. 
Winners in the acoustical group 
were Douglas Miedt, Jr. of St. Louis 
with top prize, followed by Angel 
Anastos of Chicago, Miguel Aparicio 
of Honduras, and Tommy Jones of 
Nashville. 
Winners in the electric class were 
Jimmy Miller, Hialeah, Florida, Fred 
Hamilton, Denver, John Pell, Boston 
and Joe Schuler of Winston-Salem. 
RCA Signs Mongrels 
New Canadian Group 
NEW YORK - RCA Records has 
signed the new Canadian rock group, 
The Mongrels, to an exclusive record- 
ing contract. The group comes from 
Winnipeg in 
Manitoba, the 
home 
grounds of RCA's The Guess Who, 
and were discovered about three years 
ago by Randy Bachman. Bachman, 
who until recently was part of The 
Guess Who and coauthored all of that 
group's initial hit singles, is currently 
producing The Mongrels' debut Victor 
album which is scheduled for a fall 
release. 
The Mongrels, as a group has had 
great success playing locally in the 
Winnipeg area and has performed 
often on network television and radio 
in Canada. Last year, the group was 
asked to play a guest appearance with 
the Winnipeg Symphony Orchestra- 
only the second rock group after The 
Guess Who to receive such an in- 
vitation. 
Phase II is an expansion of the 
Prophesy roster itself. Artists signed 
by Don Altfeld, A&R director, during 
the past two weeks include Charlie 
Starr, a blind singer/guitarist; The 
Elves, a six -man rock group; Nancy 
Vale, the label's first female vocalist; 
and The Groupe, five Memphis studio 
musicians. 
Both Starr and The Elves are East 
Coast groups and will be produced 
in New York. Altfeld, who is talking 
to several producers in the East, 
will fly back to make final decisions 
as to production. 
Nancy Vale is being produced by 
Altfeld 
and 
Prophesy 
President 
Mickey Shapiro with first product 
slated for mid -September. 
The Groupe will, according to Alt- 
feld, serve several purposes in ad- 
dition to recording under its own 
name. The five members are studio 
musicians and they'll be utilized on 
sessions for Prophesy acts in addition 
to traveling as a back-up group for 
Black Pearl, another of the label's 
acts. 
Since Prophesy opened its doors 
more than two months ago, Altfeld 
has traveled more than 10,000 miles 
to listen and talk to talent. 
Hoffman Acquires 
British Film Rights 
NEW YORK - Jay K. Hoffman 
Presentations Inc. has just acquired 
exclusive U. S. rights to two new 
British -produced properties, "Super- 
show," a non-stop 93 minutes of all- 
star jazz and rock music, and "Now 
That the Buffalo's Gone," a color 
documentation of the American In- 
dian. 
Both projects have application for 
either motion picture exhibitors or 
television. 
"Supershow" 
brings 
to 
the screen Eric Clapton, Roland Kirk, 
the Modern Jazz Quartet, Steve Stills, 
Led Zeppelin, Dallas Taylor, Colos- 
seum, Buddy Guy and Duster Bennett, 
among numerous others. 
"Now That the Buffalo's Gone," 
depiction of the plight of the Amer- 
ican Indian, is narrated by Marlon 
Brando, with music by Buffy Sainte 
Marie and production by Thames 
Television. The film, suitable for use 
as a single unit or in three parts, 
received strongly favorable reviews 
during its premiere screening earlier 
this year in England.

NASHVILLE - The Board of Gov- 
ernors of the Atlanta Chapter of the

meeting, selected the site for the Sep- 
tember 11-13 NARAS Trustees meet-

an executive

forthcoming Atlanta meeting. 
The Atlanta Chapter has selected 
the Royal Coach Motor Inn as the 
hostelry for the semi-annual Trustees 
meeting. Atlanta's Board

ernors voted unanimously in favor

LeFevre, vice president; Mary Tal- 
lent, secretary; 
and John 
Barbe, 
treasurer. 
Chaisson In Regional 
Ampex Promo Position 
NEW YORK - Stanley Chaisson has 
been named southern regional promo- 
tion director for Ampex 
Records, 
based in New Orleans at 3000 Gen- 
tilly Boulevard. 
He joins Ampex Records after five 
years with All South Distributors in 
New Orleans. Prior to that Chaisson 
handled independent promotion for 
A & M and Dunhill Records in the 
Southern area. 
Chaisson's responsibility at Ampex 
includes sales and promotion in Flor- 
ida, the Carolinas, Georgia, Tennes- 
see, and Texas. 
He has been a producer for Bell 
and Columbia Records.

Rosencrantz To 
LP Post At Merc 
CHICAGO - Denny Rosencrantz, 
former national promo director for 
Uni Records, has been named national 
promo manager for Albums by Mer- 
cury Records. 
Rosencrantz, 
stationed 
at 
Mer- 
cury's 
Chicago headquarters, 
will 
work closely with John Antoon, the 
company's national promo manager 
for singles. The two will report to 
Lou Simon, senior VP and director 
of marketing and sales. 
In his new post, Rosencrantz will 
be responsible for promo efforts on 
behalf of all Mercury family LPs, 
excluding the classical line. He also 
will work closely with the corpora- 
tion staff of local promotion managers 
and regional sales directors. 
Rosencrantz started in the record 
industry in 1964 as promo director 
for ABC Tape and Sales in Seattle. 
In 1968, he joined Uni and remained 
with the label until April of this 
year. 
Since then he has been co -manager 
of the Ballin' Jack rock group, new 
Columbia act, and has worked cut of 
Billy Graham's Sunny Management 
in L.A.

Dave Clark Five 
Go Separate Ways 
NEW YORK - After seven years 
in which they played a big role in 
rock hits, the Dave Clark Five have 
split. Out of the p.a. scene for two 
years, the group felt it was time 
for each member to go out in his 
own. Yet, Clark and organist Mike 
Smith may release disks together. 
The English group was a consistent 
hit -maker for Epic Records in the 
U. S. Its global sales are estimated 
at 35 million. 
Gollender To Saturday 
NEW YORK - Walt Gollender has 
joined Saturday Music, the publishing 
arm of the Crewe Group of Com- 
panies, as a member of the promo 
staff. He'll expand the unit's catalog 
of songs by Larry Brown and Ray 
Bloodworth.

B.B. King: Humming In A Major 
P.A., Promotional Campaign 
NEW YORK-B. B. King's career is 
in for a major boost on a number of 
fronts. 
The vet blues star is presently a 
Top 100 artist with his ABC/Dun- 
hill recording of "Hummingbird." One 
facet of the various promotional ac- 
tivities on King will come from the 
promo force of the label. 
In another area, the Gibson Guitar 
Co. has also been focusing on the 
performer, with full -page ads and 
other tie-ins. There's also much TV 
exposure being generated. He's ap- 
peared on the Dick Cavett Show, To- 
night the David Frost, Della Reese, 
Barbara McNair shows and on educa- 
tional TV's "Sesame Street," among 
other network, local, syndicated and 
educational 
video presentations. 
A 
highlight on Oct. 18 is a scheduled 
appearance on the Ed Sullivan Show. 
As for King's management com- 
pany, SAS, Inc., headed by Sidney 
Seidenberg, plans call for such pro- 
motional activities as the distribution 
of article reprints, photos, books and 
other materials. Full -page ads have 
also been placed in a variety of peri- 
odicals. 
To strengthen the promo drive, 
SAS has just retained the west coast 
public relations firm of Jay Bern- 
stein Associates in Hollywood to rep- 
resent King. Victoria Lucas Asso- 
ciates of New York had previously 
been named for pr. 
SHOWING THEIR `FACE': A new vocal foursome, The Face Of The Earth,

ordinator; Face Of The Earth, Sandy Patton, Mike Hawkins, Carole Holiday,

Denis Dunn, Odeon's A&R man, 
who 
recently returned 
from the 
Honolulu Convention of Capitol Rec- 
ords, reported to Cash Box the start 
of a promotion campaign in Argen- 
tina in behalf of the new artists 
presented by the diskery at that 
gathering. Dunn was greatly im- 
pressed in Hawaii by the artistic 
diversification plans by Capitol, the 
opening of offices in other US cities 
than the West Coast, and the expan- 
sion into new repertoires. 
RCA's Palito Ortega has returned 
from a new and succesful European 
tour, and was present last week at 
the premiere of one of his lateest 
films, "The Crazy Years," at the At- 
las Theater; the day before he had 
traveled to Montevideo, Uruguay, for 
the initial showing in that city. The 
diskery has recently released his LP 
recorded in Rome and London, and 
he has been also leading the "Sotano 
Beat" TV'er, on Channel 13, one of 
the top rated musical programs in 
this country. 
Leo 
Bentivoglio 
of 
Phonogram 
sends word about the special promo- 
tion campaign to be started by the 
diskery, in cooperation with the War- 
ner Bros. affiliated in this country, in 
behalf of the film and three -record 
set "Woodstock." Since the album 
has been selling very well in the 
States, it is expected that it will ride 
the charts here, too. Bentivoglio is 
also happy with the success of the 
recent 
Bee Gees waxing, "Io -Io," 
which is selling very well and ap- 
pears this week on the local charts. 
Mauricio Breneer of Fermata sends 
word about the publishing of "Nos 
Amamos," the French original tune 
which is appearing in the charts 
through several artists, and the re- 
lease of the Noi Giovani version of 
the tune. The diskery is also promot- 
ing the recent LP by Italian chan - 
tress Mina, recorded originally on the 
PDU label. 
Korn 
Publishers 
are controlling 
three of the winners of the recent TV 
Song Fest. organized by Channel 18. 
The titles are "Sembremos Paz y 
Amor por los Caminos," composed 
and sung by Elio Roca (Polydor), 
"Coplas de los Anos Maduros," sung 
by Gabino Correa, and "Las Paredes 
y el Verde de Mi Ciudad," by Sergio 
Villar Junior. 
Music Hall's Calvo infos about tan- 
go maestro Jose Basso leading the 
Argentine Evening Gala at the "Fes- 
tival Plaza" of the Expo 70 showing 
in Osaka, Japan. The Ambassador of 
this country to Japan was present at 
the recital, which was extremely suc- 
cesful. Basso has been fulfilling con- 
tracts in that market and will now 
return to Buenos Aires. 
CBS' Piombi informs about the re- 
lease of the new single by Sandro, 
"Pobre Mi Madre Querida," which 
has initial orders for 50,000 copies 
and sems to be a new hit in the 
chanter's career. The label is selling 
strongly the first album by Amelita 
Baltar, and also the new single by

GRT Holds Toronto Meet 
GRT of Canada's second year of op- 
eration was celebrated with a four - 
day meeting in Toronto involving all 
their distributors from across Cana- 
da. Base of the meetings was the 
posh Guild 'Inn on Lake Ontario in 
the Scarborough suburb of Toronto. 
Opening night (3), 
a holiday in 
Canada, GRT provided a hospitality 
suite to allow visitors the opportuni- 
ty of meeting with head office staff. 
Morris Levy, of Roulette Records, 
flew in for the occasion along with 
one of the label's top money makers, 
Don Cooper. After the usual round 
of handshakes Cooper entertained in 
a sort of campfire arrangement, one 
which he obviously enjoyed as well 
as his audience. 
The next two days were devoted to 
a workshop series of meetings, over- 
seen by 
the company's 
president, 
Ross Reynolds and his national sales 
manager, Ed LaBuick. 
Capper for the meeting was a large 
sized blowout at the Avenue Road 
Club, 
in 
the 
heart of Toronto's 
Yorkville Village. Teagarten and Van 
Winkle opened the show attended by 
all GRT employees and distributors 
along with invited members of radio, 
press and key dealers. Alive and 
Kicking, a Roulette group, were ex- 
ceptionally good, although the room 
wasn't the best acoustically. This 
group, now heading for the top of 
the 
nation's 
charts 
with 
their 
"Tighter & Tighter" deck, worked fe - 
Polyflor Acts Set U.K. Tour 
Polydor's Stone The Crows and 
Jake Holmes will be joining Atoo 
blues group Taste on a major tour of 
the U.K. 
and continental 
Europe 
starting September 
6. 
The 
tour, 
which includes dates in twelve major 
British cities, has been organized by 
Polydor Records, London, and co- 
ordinated by publicity chief Clive 
Woods. 'It will 
coincide with the 
worldwide release of new albums by 
Stone The Crows and Holmes. 
Jake Holmes first visited Europe 
earlier this year to promote his first 
album for Polydor, "Jake Holmes," 
and he appeared extensively on radio 
and television, and at a number of 
concerts together with Taste, who are 
a 
major attraction 
in 
European 
venues. He is also known as the co - 
writer 
of Frank Sinatra's 
recent 
"Watertown" album. 
Appearing with Holmes will be 
New York guitarist Teddy Irwin and 
a European backing group.

dynamic Funkedelics and Parliaments 
followed with what must have been a 
solid hour of "high" delivery with a 
fantastic lighting effect that got to 
some of the crowd but couldn't come 
close to the excitement they were 
able to generate with the Montreal 
crowd witnessed by this correspon- 
dent, last year.

AFM Members OK New TV Net Pact 
NEW YORK, N.Y.-Ratification of a 
new two-year contract between the 
American Federation of Musicians 
(AFL-CIO), and the television net- 
works has been announced by Federa- 
tion president Hal C. Davis. 
The vote on the new contract was 
497 to 78. AFM members working in 
television were polled in major pro- 
duction centers by secret ballot. In 
all, 
1199 ballots were mailed 
to 
affected musicians, Davis said. 
Highlights of the pact, which is 
retroactive to Aug. 1, 1970 and ex- 
pires July 31, 1972, are: 
Wages for casual musicians in- 
creased 12% in the basic air rate from 
$34.10 to 
$38.19 for 
a half-hour 
show; up from $44 to $49.28 for an 
hour show; and from $66 to $73.92 
for shows of 90 minutes. Twelve per 
cent increases also for additional 
time, and in participating sponsor 
rates. Rehearsal rates for casual mu- 
sicians have been raised from $13.42 
to $15 per hour. The rate on the 
hour-long variety special increased 
from $13.42 to $15.50, beginning with 
the 16th hour. 
In addition, wage increases of 12 
per cent now apply to the rates for 
music preparation work and for re- 
hearsal musicians. 
Major Gain Cited 
An important gain for musicians, 
Davis said, is a commitment by the 
networks that they will furnish to 
the Federation, within 30 days of the 
effective date of the contract, a list of 
all shows using music, and the pro- 
ducer of each show. Further, they 
will require each outside packager of 
a show to sign an agreement or a 
letter of adherence with the AFM. 
"This 
is extremely important 
in 
terms of policing both the domestic 
re -use and foreign -use provisions of 
our contracts," Davis said.

contract are: calls shall be only for 
one specific show; more advance no-

other

More 'Sesame St.' 
Visits By Columbia 
NEW YORK - Columbia Records 
has released six original cast book 
and 
record 
sets 
from 
"Sesame 
Street." The 45 rpm records, pack- 
aged in gaily colored board books 
which feature and illustrate the lyrics 
sung on the accompanying record, 
will be released this month following 
the initial "Sesame Street" LP re- 
leased by the company. 
Project director Arthur Simkin at 
Columbia, and Tom Shepard, pro- 
ducer for Columbia, worked closely 
with staff members of the Children's 
Television Workshop, producers of 
the "Sesame Street" series, to create 
the most authentic and appealing 
visual and listening package pos- 
sible. 
Each of the six -record sets carries 
a suggested retail price of $.99. The 
entire set of six is packaged in a 
colorful cardboard carry -about with 
a leatherette carrying handle. The 
suggested retail price for the entire 
set is $4.98. 
The records contain thirteen of the 
songs and linking dialogues penned 
for the series by Joe Raposo, Jeffrey 
Moss, 
and 
Jon 
Stone 
("Sesame 
Street" b/w "Hello," "Goin' For A 
Ride" b/w "I Love Trash", "ABC- 
DEFGHI" b/w "J -Jump", "One of 
These Things' b/w "Up And Down", 
"People In Your Neighborhood" b/w 
"Somebody Come And Play", and 
"Number 5" and "Five People In My 
Family" b/w "I've Got Two". They 
are sung by "Sesame Street" cast 
members Matt Robinson (Gordon), 
Loretta Long (Susan), Bob McGrath 
(Bob), Will Lee (Mr. Hopper), the 
adorable Muppets (created by Jim 
Henson), and the remarkable group 
of children who play such a vital role 
in the series. 
The accompanying colored books, 
illustrated by Brian Cranner, contain 
the full lyrics to each of the songs on 
the record. It allows the listener to 
follow the songs on record and sing 
along with the cast. 
Columbia 
has 
designed 
several 
floor -and -counter 
display 
merchan- 
diser -units which will be utilized by 
thousands of retailers throughout the 
country to facilitate rapid turnover 
of the sets. The displays incorporate 
the 
artwork 
used 
on 
both 
the 
"Sesame Street" television show and 
the record -set artwork. 
Additional "Sesame Street" materi- 
al is planned for future release by 
Columbia. Three additional book and 
record sets are scheduled for release 
in late Fall, with more to follow. 
Goody Half-Yr Report 
MASPETH, NEW YORK - Sam 
Goody, Inc. has reported the results 
of operations for the first half and 
twelve months ended June 30, 1970. 
Earnings for the first six months 
of 1970 amounted to $90,306, or $.13 
per share, calculated on 
683,000 
shares, as compared with $74,489, or 
$.11 per share on 650,000 shares, for 
the comparable six months of 1969. 
Sales of the company for the 1970 
first half amounted to a record $9,- 
876,860, as compared with $6,930,992 
reported in the same 1969 period. 
,For the trailing twelve months 
ended June 30, sales amounted to 
$19,176,651, as compared with $14,- 
901,866 recorded in the comparable 
twelve months through June 
30, 
1969. Earnings rose to $636,073, or 
$.95 per share, as compared with 
$412,689, or $.68 per share for the 
respective twelve month periods. 
Per share results for the 1969 peri- 
ods have been adjusted for the 2 -for - 
1 stock split in December, 1969. 
Sam Goody, president, noted that 
start-up costs in connection with es- 
tablishment of the new wholesale di- 
vision, as well as interest expenses 
incurred in financing the acquisition, 
prevented first half earnings from 
expanding further. 
Goody indicated that the compa- 
ny's ninth retail store is scheduled 
for opening in September in the 
regional King's Plaza Shopping Cen- 
ter in 'Brooklyn, New York, and that 
the company's 10th unit would be 
located in a large shopping center 
being constructed 
in 
Woodbridge, 
New Jersey, which is scheduled for 
completion by next spring. 
Sam Goody, Inc. (O.T!C.) presently 
operates a chain of eight retail audio 
and record stores. Through a wholly - 
owned subsidiary, Brun -International 
Recotape Corporation, the company 
is also engaged in the wholesale dis- 
tribution of records, tapes and ac- 
cessories.

Mfg Services Mgr. 
NEW YORK - Joe Gowan, vice presi- 
dent in charge of administration, has 
announced the appointment of Janie 
Gans as manager of manufacturing 
services for the GRT Record Group.

mechanical aspects of the production

Joe Louis Fete 
Raises $75,000 
NEW YORK - The night of Aug. 12 
at Detroit's Cobo Hall, "Salute to 
The Champ-Joe Louis," has resulted 
in a purse in trust for the boxing 
great of more than $75,000, and could 
easily reach six figures. The finance 
committee said donations to help 
Louis, a patient at the Denver Veter- 
an's Hospital, are still pouring into 
the special address set aside for this 
purpose: Salute to The Champ-Joe 
Louis, Bank of the Commonwealth, 
P.O. Box 
3156, Detroit, Michigan 
48231. 
Motown president Berry Gordy, Jr., 
honorary chairman of the event, and 
an ex -fighter himself who once fought 
on the same card with Joe Louis, made 
the dream of the Salute come true 
when he marshalled his vast resources 
in manpower, show business acumen 
and leadership, just a few short weeks 
prior to the event. 
Gordy said: "To see the smile on 
Joe's face when he learns how his 
friends throughout the nation, and 
particularly in Detroit, rallied to his 
side in his time of need, not just with 
sincere sentiment, but with dollars, is 
a vision which will be with me as long 
as I live." 
Executive Directors of the Salute 
were Detroiters Rosa Owens and Jose- 
phine Winfrey. 
O'Keefe Vanguard's 
National Promo Man 
NEW YORK - Eddie O'Keefe has 
been appointed national promo direc- 
tor of Vanguard Records, effective 
immediately, according to Herb Cor - 
sack, vice-president in charge of sales 
and promo. 
O'Keefe comes to Vanguard after 
three years as a local promo man for 
Mercury Records. His move to Van- 
guard will give him an opportunity to 
join forces, again, with Bob Reno, 
Vanguard's Director of pop A&R. 
While at Mercury, O'Keefe was asso- 
ciated with such hits as "Na Na Hey 
Hey Kiss Him Goodbye" and "Je 
T'Aime'' for Reno. Prior to his posi- 
tion at Mercury, O'Keefe worked as a 
local promo man for Globe Distrib- 
utors and Delta Records. 
O'Keefe will be on the road meeting 
with local DJ's, distributors and 
promo men for his first three months 
at Vanguard. He will then be based in 
New York, reporting to Corsack. 
In making the announcement of the 
appointment Corsack said, "With the 
acquisition of O'Keefe we've taken a 
major step in furthering Vanguard's 
involvement in the 'top 40' market."

Air Lecuona Specials 
NEW YORK - Edward B. Marks 
Music, reports that several radio sta- 
tions across the country, including 
WAIT, WMAQ, WEFF and WNUS in 
Chicago and WNEW, WNYC, WPAT 
and WHM in the New York area, 
have agreed to broadcast special pro- 
grams based on Ernesto Lecuona's 
music to celebrate his 75th birth an- 
niversary this month. Arrangements 
are also being made to release new 
recordings of his works. 
Composer 
of "Andalucia" 
(The 
Breeze and 1), "Malaguena", "La 
Comparsa", "Canto Karabali" (Jun- 
gle Drums), "Para Vigo Me Voy" 
(Say 'Si Si') and hundreds of other 
songs and works for piano, orchestra 
and band, Lecuona was among those 
few composers who have achieved 
great successes in both serious and 
popular music fields. 
A discography of Lecuona's works, 
recently brought out by Edward B. 
Marks Music, which includes only the 
records released in U. S. A., lists 240 
recordings 
under "Andalucia" and 
225 
under "Malaguena." 
And the 
most recent record catalog of E. B. 
Marks Music shows that with 
25 
disks "Malaguena" was the third 
most recorded song in the catalog 
during the last year, while "Andalu- 
cia" with 17 waxings occupied the 9th 
place.

New KSON Editorials 
SAN DIEGO - A new system of 
community involvement and method 
to answer editorials has been de- 
veloped by KSON. 
When 
station 
president Dan McKinnon editorial- 
izes, after his comments, listeners are 
urged to call a telephone number and 
have their response, pro or con to the 
editorial, recorded on telephone com- 
pany equipment. 
The listener's statements are then 
re-recorded on regular tape and re- 
broadcast the following day in the 
editorial slots. A different person's 
viewpoint is broadcast at each time 
the 
editorial 
was 
broadcast 
the 
preceding day. When an individual is 
named in an editorial, he is searched 
out to provide the rebuttal comment.

Schaffer Promo Firm 
Debuts In Frisco 
SAN FRANCISCO - Gary Schaffer, 
former KYA music director, has an- 
nounced the formation of Schaffer 
Associates, a total concept indepen- 
dent promotion firm, with headquar- 
ters in San Francisco. 
Joining Schaffer in the organiza- 
tion are Pam Burns and Judy Levy. 
The trio will concentrate on product 
service to media, artist relations, dis- 
tributor, rack one stop, and retail 
coordination. "In short, we'll give 
our clients an outfit to depend on in 
one of America's top five markets," 
Schaffer said. 
Schaffer left announcing and music 
duties at KYA last March and spent 
the intervening months touring the 
country, visiting potential 
clients, 
and seeking new talent and masters.

Hendrix Launches 
Electric Lady 
NEW YORK - Super star Jimi Hen- 
drix has arrived in New York in anti- 
cipation of the August 26 opening of 
his recording studio, Electric Lady at 
52 West Eighth Street. Electric Lady 
contains two studios, the larger of 
which has 36 tracks and is acoustical- 
ly divided into a live and dead side of 
the room. Other facilities 
of the 
studio include colored lights, a moog 
synthesizer, and a plush decor which 
is consistent with the Hendrix image. 
The studio was designed by Eddy 
Kramer, chief engineer. Maintenance 
Engineer is Shimon Ron and Kim 
King is the second engineer. Jon 
Storyk was the architect of the 
studio which is managed by Jim Mar- 
ron. Electric Lady has already been 
used by several artists including Buzz 
Linhart Elliot Randall, Irene Reid, 
Glory River, Hendrix himself and 
Led Zeppelin, who mixed their latest 
LP there. 
Capitol Pacts Deal 
With North Star 
HOLLYWOOD - Capitol Records 
Inc., has entered into an independent 
production agreement with 
North 
Star Productions of Berkeley Califor- 
nia. According to the agreement ar- 
ranged by Ed Denson and producer 
John Palladino, Capitol is to recieve 
the masters recorded by the five 
member group Joy Of Cooking. Their 
first album for the label is being 
readied for release.

BUDDAH FALL PRODUCT PRE- 
SENTATION - Buddah 
Records 
kicked off their east coast album 
presentation of fall product with a 
luncheon held at the Playboy Club in 
New York City. Performing at the 
luncheon were Curtom Records' rec- 
ording stars, The Impressions and 
Kama Sutra recording artists, Brewer 
& 
Shipley 
who 
entertained 
the 
gathered audience of east coast dis- 
tributors, representatives from Bud- 
dah distributed labels, and several in- 
dependent promotion men. Art Kass, 
Co -President 
of 
the Buddah/Kama 
Sutra group of labels, explained to 
the distributors present at the lunch- 
eon the significance of this years' 
limited number of fall releases. "We 
believe that it is the quality; not the 
quantity that determines the success 
of the label," said Kass. The fall LP 
releases include: a new Melanie al- 
bum recorded live at Carnegie Hall; a 
new Brooklyn Bridge album; Curtis 
Mayfield's first solo album; and Im- 
pressions' album including both their 
hit "Check Out Your Mind" and their 
new single , "Baby Turn Me On;" 
three albums from the Sussex label: 
"Mutzie," "Dennis Coffey And The 
Detroit Guitar Band," and "Priscil- 
la;" "Wahonka" on Super K Records; 
"Head," an electronic sounds album 
which includes a coloring book; a 
re -issue of the 
original 
"Captain 
Beefheart And His Magic Band;" 
"More Happy Days" from the Edwin 
Hawkins Singers; a first album from 
Dorothy 
Morrison; a 
new album 
from Wille Bobo; a classic "Little 
Richard" album; 
and a "Barbara 
Mason" album from National Gener- 
al Records. Prior to the slide presen- 
tation, Neil Bogart, Co -President of 
the Buddah/Kama Sutra group of la- 
bels, spoke briefly. "Is singing ille- 
gal? She asked the question as she 
broke the law by singing the song 
that thirty thousand young people 
wanted to hear. Melanie sang at the 
Powder Ridge Festival in Connecti- 
cut. She sang `There's a chance peace 
will come' and as she sang it she was 
breaking the law because half a doz- 
en politicians did not want the fes- 
tival to take place and made it illegal 
for any group to get up on the stage 
and sing their song," said Bogart 
concluding his speech by emphasizing 
the responsibility of everyone con- 
cerned in every aspect of the music 
industry toward keeping music an ex- 
pression of freedom. Shown at the 
luncheon are ABOVE (1. to r.) Mary 
Stuart, manager of the Impressions,

Cash 
of

SIMON & GARFUNKEL (Columbia 45237) 
El Condor Pasa (3:06) (Charing Cross, BMI-Arr/Lyr: Simon) 
Paul Simon's arrangement and lyrics turn a marvelous South American 
folk melody into a stunning commentary. Originally one of the highlight 
tracks in their "Bridge Over Troubled Water" LP, "El Condor now becomes 
the duo's third giant single post -released from the gold set. Flip: "Why 
Don't You Write Me" (2:45) (Same credits) 
THREE DOG NIGHT (Dunhill 4250) 
Out in the Country (3:08) (Irving, BMI-Williams, Nichols) 
Growing mellower in recent performances, Three Dog Night offers its 
softest showcase yet in this new track from the "It Ain't Easy" LP. Attrac- 
tive material and an exciting TDN delivery give the team another top forty 
blockbuster, one that might even become an MOR breakthrough. Flip: "Good 
Time Living" (4:06) (Screen Gems/Columbia, BMI-Mann, Weil) 
THE DELFONICS (Philly Groove 163) 
When You Get Right Down to It (2:48) Screen Gems/Columbia, BMI-Mann) 
Brighter and brighter with each successive performance, the Delfonics 
drift home with this dreamy ballad. Sparkling vocal style and a grand pro- 
duction give the team an astonishing piece of work with this powerful piece 
of material. One of the group's strongest. Flip: no info. 
WHITE PLAINS (Deram 85066) 
Lovin' You Baby (3:05) (Maribus, BMI-Cook, Greenaway) 
The "My Baby Loves Lovin' " team comes back with yet another sample 
of their teen electricity in this follow-up outing. Working with the rhythmic 
sugar of their first, and topping it with tasty vocals, the White Plains takes 
off for round two on the top forty charts. Flip: "Noises (in My Head") 
(3:15) (Same credits) 
MOUNTAIN (Windfall 533) 
For Yasgur's Farm (3:20) (Upfall, ASCAP-Gardos, Laing, Pappalardi, Col- 
lins, Ship, Rea) 
Considerably different from the group's "Mississippi Queen" hit, this 
new Mountain offering subdues its rhythmic drive for a more lyrical venture. 
Based on FM play from the "Climbing" album, this track should maintain 
Mountain's range over the top forty charts. Flip: "To My Friend" (3:38) 
(Upfall, ASCAP-West) 
THE THREE DEGREES (Roulette 7088) 
I Do Take You (3:07) (Planetary/Make, ASCAP-March) 
With their last release the Three Degrees showed it was no "Maybe," 
but a certainty. Now, the trio focuses on new material that carries even 
greater top forty impact to assure tremendous dual -market sales. Excellent 
ballad is superbly performed here to establish the group as regulars on the 
best seller lists. Flip: no info. 
TOMMY ROE (ABC 11273) 
We Can Make Music (2:50) (Little Fugitive, BMI-Josie) 
One of Roe's strongest commercial efforts in a long while, this entry 
should bust the artist into the top forty charts without the months of work 
that were needed for his last handful. Excellent teen outing which has the 
instant impact of a winner. Flip: no info. 
R.B. GREAVES (Atco 6778) 
Georgia Took Her Back (2:37) (Cuddles/Cotillion, BMI-Rowlands) 
Though his "Take a Letter Maria" was self -composed, R.B. Greaves has 
followed up by material from other writers. Now, he turns to yet another 
pen for his third shot at chart fame. Bright, bristling ballad in a style 
reminiscent of his own first hit gives Greaves a powerful teen sound. Flip: 
no infor. 
BILLY JOE ROYAL (Columbia 45220) 
Every Night (3:12) (Maclen, BMI-McCartney) 
Excellent revamping of the "McCartney" track gives Billy Joe Royal yet 
another sparkler to pace him into the top forty picture. Paying even more 
attention to the lyric than the original. Royal makes this gem a standout 
choice for top forty programming. Flip: "Burning a Hole" (2:50) (Low -Sal, 
BMI-Buie, Cobb) 
JAKE HOLMES (Polydor 14041) 
So Close (3:26) (Out of Business, ASCAP-Holmes) 
Dropping the sting of his earlier performances, Jake Holmes turns in a 
masterful ballad here that should bring him his first taste of top forty and 
MOR excitement as an artist. Exquisitely written, tenderly sung and pro- 
duced with a luster. Flip: "Django & Friend" (3:37) (Same credits) 
CHARLES RANDOLPH GREAN SOUNDE (Ranwood 880) 
AL DeLORY (Capitol 2902) 
Theme from "Borsalino" (2:19/2:30) (Famous, ASCAP-Bolling) 
Two of the leading instrumental groups currently riding the singles circuit 
both lock horns in a race with the theme from "Borsalino." Generally strong 
reviews for the newly opened Delain/Belmondo movie are bound to stimu- 
late audiences. DeLory's version is closer to the soundtrack playing, and 
comes behind his "M -A -S -H" hit. Charles Randolph Grean, though, speeds 
the tempo for a more contemporary approach and has a few days edge on 
the marketing. 
SONNY CHARLES (A&M 1214) 
Half as Much (2:45) (Acuff -Rose, BMI-Williams) 
In no way reminiscent of the long -gone original, Sonny Charles' updating 
of "Half as Much" turns the song into a contemporary piece which couples 
his electric vocal with a rhythmic power that should return him to the top 
forty and R&B charts again. Another "Pearl" for the man. Flip: "Will You Be 
Easy" (3:05) (Good Friday/Black Pearl, BMI-Shelton) 
THE HONEY CONE (Hot Wax 7005) 
When Will It End (2:46) (Gold Forever, BMI-Dunbar, Wayne) 
Moving into high -gear immediately, the Honey Cone sets up an emotional 
tension that keeps the listener enthralled to the very end. Powerfully pro- 
duced and performed, "When Will It End" should boom into top forty charts 
and amass a top forty action on top. Flip: "Take Me With You" (2:55) 
(Same credits) 
(Newcomer Picks 
ANDRA WILLIS (Paramount 0048) 
Knock, Knock Who's There (2:25) (Peer Intl, BMI-Carter,Stephens) 
Delghtful femme vocal work with a twinkle matches the giddy musical 
quality of a bright new song. Side is taken from a Mary Hopkin charter in 
the United Kingdom and has already begun to spread the sales in the U.S. 
through strong initial radio response. Flip: no info. 
DIANE KOLBY (Columbia 45169) 
Holy Man (3:05) (Fodderwing, ASCAP-Kolby) 
Vocally mixing the textures of Gracie Slick and Dionne Warwick, this new 
powerhouse embodied by Diane Kolby presents a pulverizing new talent to 
shatter top forty and FM networks. Stunningly showcaced in this original 
song, Miss Kolby carries the aural magnetism to assure stardom. Flip: no 
info. 
THE UTOPIA PARKWAY (United Artists 50690) 
Come With Me (2:48) (Red Canyon/U.A., ASCAP-Brodsky, Drago, Espo- 
sito, Tourso) 
The message of "Leaving on a Jet Plane" and a gentle delivery turn the 
Utopia Parkway's first release into a majestic ballad with exciting appeal for 
both top forty and middle-of-the-road stations. Already on the playlists at 
several important stations, the record has taken its first steps toward the 
best seller list. Flip: "I Don't Understand You" (2:23) (Red Candle/U.A., 
ASCAP-Drago) 
THE AL CAPPS BAND (Columbia 45219) 
Odyssey Rock Park (2:57) (Canopy, ASCAP-Webb, Strauss) 
Latinization of the "Thus Spake Zarathustra" motif of "2001" and its 
incorporation with the "Macarthur Park" melody gives the Al Capps Band 
a mind -shattering work. The combo's originality and choice material should 
make this a rapid top forty climber. Flip: No info. 
BILLY PEEK (White Whale 357) 
It Came Out of the Sky (2:39) (Jondora, BMI-Fogerty) 
A song that gained exposure from Creedence Clearwater's LP version, "It 
Came Out of the Sky" now appears in its first single performance, and a 
spirited one it is. Keeping the CCR rhythm and arrangement fairly intact, 
Billy Peek's treatment carries enough impact to make it a top forty long 
shot on the way home. Flip: "Population Explosion" (2:25) (Lone Wolf, 
BMI-Ross, Johnston)

Popp Best Bets 
THE BEST OF JOSH WHITE - Elektra 75008 
Twenty-five years of Josh White's perform- 
ances on records are distilled into a magnifi- 
cent tribute to the artist in this collection. The 
two -disk package includes not only 21 songs 
but a full -side musical narrative version of 
White's classic "Story of John Henry." Material 
for the collection was taken from tapes during 
the 1955-62 peak of White's career, and fea- 
tures "Sam Hall," "Jesus Gonna Make Up My 
Dyin' Bed" and "Midnight Special" among 
others. Beautifully packaged, the set is also 
being merchandised to retail at a $5.98 list for 
added consumer enticement. 
THE USE OF ASHES - Pearls Before Swine 
- Reprise 6405 
Devotees of the unusual and daring in 
musical forms, take heart. The new Pearls 
Before Swine album is here. Latest effort by 
Tom Rapp and his companions could easily 
catapult them into the wide pop appeal area 
which has thus far eluded them. From the 
hypnotic "The Jeweler" to the strange and 
beautiful "Rocket Man," based on 
a short 
story by Ray Bradbury, this is an LP of taste 
and special quality. Rapp's distinctive vocal 
style is brought to bear on some of his most 
poetic compositions to date. A class LP. 
THE BEATLES ALBUM - Percy Faith Strings 
- Columbia 30097 
Although the Beatles have broken up, their 
songs are still very much together as is evi- 
denced by this beautiful package of eleven 
Beatle standards ably played by the Percy 
Faith Strings. Included in the album are two 
recent Beatle hits, "Let it Be" and "Some- 
thing" along with old favorites "Eleanor Rig- 
by," "Michelle," "Fool on the Hill," and 
a 
host of other immortals. 
UP ABOVE OUR HEADS - Clouds - Deram 
18044 
Here's an interesting album by a hard rock 
trio from Scotland. The group penned six of 
the eight cuts on the LP including "In The 
Mine" on which drummer Harry Hughes dou- 
bles very capably on trumpet. Other heavies 
include "Imagine Me," which contains some 
very interesting vocal lines, and a thirteen min- 
ute plus jazz version of "Sing, Sing. Sing." 
Definitely worth a listen. 
MAGICIAN - ANDREW LEIGH - Sire 97025 
Andrew Leigh and company provide an al- 
bum chock full of interesting songs and ar- 
rangements that should make for some very 
easy listening. Along with Leigh and 
Kevin 
Westlake (who wrote the entire album) the 
other musicians provide 
a first rate 
back- 
ground for nine simply beautiful songs. Could 
be a big chart item if it catches on. 
THE CUFF LINKS - Decca DL -75235 
The Cuff Links are headed for the top of 
the charts with this album. The nine member 
group have come up with eleven beautifully 
written cuts with the emphasis on love and 
the women (Robin, Jennifer, Bobbie, and Sal- 
ly) who inspire it. Should be a good seller.

Maurer Cancels 
Donovan Tour 
NEW YORK-Sid Maurer, Donovan's personal 
rep, has issued a statement regarding the can- 
cellation rumors of the Scottish folk singer's 
American tour which was scheduled to begin 
in mid November. "We've had some change in 
plans regarding Donovan's American tour. 
He 
will be taking a much deserved rest, and will 
confine his activities to some of the projects 
he would otherwise not have time to complete. 
By using the alloted time, which would have 
taken him through the end of this year, he 
will concentrate on finishing a 2 record Chil- 
dren's Album; doing 
a 
non-profit anti drug 
film; performing a series of free concerts for 
children; and in finishing a book of poetry." 
The American fall Tour is now set for Spring 
of 1971."
